1jtlv76:280: The design of Review Agent is fundamentally about fully decoupling the roles of "executor" and "evaluator." This decoupling is not intuitive in engineering, because letting the same model both do the work and review it seems more resource-efficient. But winty points out a counterintuitive fact in the article: during self-evaluation, the sunk cost of execution suppresses the objectivity of evaluation—an Agent finds it hard to give negative feedback on its own work, because that conflicts with the execution mindset of "I just did my best." This psychological mechanism holds for both humans and models, which is why Hermes chose physical isolation: one Agent runs the task, another Agent reviews. Independent review improves hit rate on subsequent tasks by about 3x compared to self-reflection, strongly validating the necessity of this design.

If every review creates a new entry instead of merging updates, the same fact gets recorded multiple times, versions contradict each other, and retrieval quality eventually degrades. 69miw:272: If the Nudge Engine is Hermes' "switch," then the Review Agent is its "mind." The design I admire most when reading Hermes' source code is this part. This seems like a small thing, but it solves a very fundamental engineering problem: having someone currently working judge how well they just did always results in something long, self-congratulatory, and useless. The Review Agent solves exactly this problem.
